subject: BlueWave Health pricing + cross-region billing questions
messages:
From: Jaspreet Singh <j.singh@bluewavehealth.com>

Cc: procurement@bluewavehealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing + region billing (RFP attached)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. We circulated your product brief internally and have two immediate asks as we prepare our formal RFP response: 1) a clear example of per-token pricing at three commit tiers (monthly token volumes) for the hosted API, and 2) how Redwood handles cross-region usage from a billing perspective — do you charge by region of model execution, by source region, or can we consolidate billing under a single HQ invoice?

To give you context: our pilot will predominantly be US traffic (~65%), with steady EU traffic (~25%) for regulatory workloads and a small APAC presence (~10%) that will grow in Q3. We expect to start with 30M tokens/month and may scale to a committed 250M tokens/month within 6–9 months if latency & cost look good.

I've attached our RFP summary (BlueWave_RFP.pdf) and the procurement form procurement@bluewavehealth.com will need filled for early procurement review. Can you get me a simple table (example tiers, per-token rates, and any regional uplift) and confirm whether committed discounts can be blended across regions?

Appreciate it — Jaspreet
Director of AI Strategy
BlueWave Health

Attachments: BlueWave_RFP.pdf

Hi Jaspreet — great to connect. Thanks for the RFP and the volume guidance. High level answers up front, then a short attachment with a worked example (pricing_model_v3.xlsx).

Summary (hosted API — standard offering):
- List pricing: $0.00036 per token for generation (baseline).
- Commit tiers (example):
  * 0–50M/mo: no commit (pay-as-you-go) at list
  * 50–200M/mo: 10% discount off list
  * 200M+/mo: 20% discount off list
- Regional uplift: EU endpoints typically have a +5% regional cost adjustment due to infra/residency; APAC +8% in some hosted regions.
- Billing scope: by default we invoice aggregated usage per account, but by-region chargebacks are available (we can either: consolidated monthly invoice with region line-items, or separate invoices per region if required).

Key clarifying questions:
1) Do you need a single global commit (one pool of committed tokens applied to all regions) or per-region minimums?
2) Is consolidated invoicing a hard procurement requirement (i.e., must be a single invoice to HQ), or would an invoice copy per legal entity suffice?

I've looped in Laura from Sales Ops who can confirm billing mechanics. I've also noted your volumes — if you commit to a 12-month global agreement at 150M tokens/mo we can put together a blended discount schedule that improves on the standard tiers.

Next step: I can send a short term-sheet and a pricing workbook. Would you like a quick call Thursday to walk through line items?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Hosted API pricing + region billing (RFP attached)

Hi Jaspreet / Aditya — adding detail from Sales Ops on how billing and region-based pricing work today. Short version: we can support consolidated billing and also apply committed discounts on a global basis, but there are operational considerations.

Operational notes:
- Chargeable metric: tokens are billed where the model inference executes (region of the serving endpoint). If you route US requests to a US endpoint and EU requests to an EU endpoint, those executions are recorded under each region for cost accounting.
- Consolidated invoice: we can produce a single monthly invoice to BlueWave HQ (US) showing aggregated spend and per-region breakout lines. This meets most procurement needs; if EU legal requires a separate invoice for VAT/regulatory purposes we can provide invoice copies per entity.
- Blended discounts: we can apply a global blended discount against an agreed global commit. Example: sign a 12-month global commit of X tokens/month; discounts are calculated on aggregate usage across regions. We recommend a small per-region minimum (e.g., 10% of commit) to ensure capacity planning.
- Data residency: for workloads marked as "EU residency required" we will pin endpoints to EU zones; those executions will be routed to EU hosts and billed as EU region usage (no cross-region egress).

I'll attach a short pricing workbook to illustrate blended vs per-region math. Aditya — if BlueWave needs a contractual term to guarantee consolidated billing and EU invoice copies, let me know and I can draft language.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing + region billing (technical & term suggestions)

Looping in a technical perspective and a suggested commercial structure that tends to work for customers with mixed-region footprints.

Technical notes:
- EU residency: we can deploy dedicated EU-hosted endpoints and pin model execution there (no egress) for any traffic flagged as EU-residency. This is standard for regulated datasets; we can provide architecture notes and an SOC2 scope excerpt.
- Routing: Redwood's routing policy supports sticky region-based routing with smart fallback to nearest compatible variant; this minimizes latency while honoring residency.

Suggested commercial model (example):
- 12-mo global commit: 150M tokens/month aggregated across regions.
- Blended discount: 18% off list across the aggregated commit (improves on standard 20% break point by smoothing tiers).
- Per-region uplifts: EU +4% on list to cover residency infra; APAC +7% if routed to higher-cost hosts. These uplifts are applied before discounting.
- Per-region minimum: 10% of committed tokens must be consumed from each active region; if a region falls below that minimum for 3 consecutive months, billing rebalancing applies (we can credit unused regional minimum into the global pool with a specified lag).
- Overage: any usage above commit billed at pay-as-you-go list rates with monthly true-ups.

Commercial ask: I propose we offer BlueWave a one-time enrollment incentive: a 1-month credit equivalent to 5% of the first month committed spend (to offset initial migration/tests). Aditya / Laura — is this approvalable within standard deal authority or do we need SDR/VP sign-off?

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

- Discount: blended 18% across the global aggregated commit.
